☕ THE LEAD

This Cyber Week, AI agents are about to go absolutely bonkers, with traffic surging an estimated 150x, mostly driven by Meta's Muse. Here's the kicker: Walmart just announced a partnership with Meta to let customers shop Black Friday deals directly through Muse, but Amazon is still in "talks" to lift its two-month blockade on the AI shopping assistant. This is a fascinating high-stakes game of chicken. On one side, Amazon worries about losing ad revenue if Muse bypasses its on-site ads and about the quality of Muse's product recommendations. On the other, Walmart is fully embracing the future, betting that meeting customers where they are (even if that's an AI agent) is the smarter play. The takeaway for marketers? Whether you're a big retailer or a small brand, you need a strategy for how AI agents interact with *your* product catalog, because consumers are clearly ready to outsource their shopping to the bots. [S20][S91][S59][S60]

📣 QUICK HITS

**AI Fatigue Pushes Brands Back to Human Craft**
As consumers get tired of AI-generated ads, brands like Geico, Coca-Cola, and Walmart are leaning into handcrafted creative and "handfuls of creators" for their holiday campaigns. It's a smart move to prioritize authentic, human-first content when everything else feels a bit too synthetic. [S4][S15]

**X Leans Hard into Vertical Video for Creators**
Elon's platform is rolling out new creation tools specifically for vertical video, clearly trying to snatch a piece of the short-form video pie from YouTube and Instagram. If you're building a creator strategy, this is a clear signal to prioritize vertical formats on X. [S50]

**GLP-1 Drugs Are Reshaping the Thanksgiving Table**
Weight-loss drugs like Ozempic, Wegovy, and Mounjaro are having a real impact on grocery shopping and holiday meal planning. Marketers in food and beverage need to pay attention to this consumer trend; it's already changing purchasing habits. [S21]

**Kraft Heinz Gets Cheesy with NFL Sponsorship**
Kraft Heinz has inked a five-year global partnership with the NFL for brands like Velveeta and Kraft Mac & Cheese. They're literally putting "cheese pylons" on the field — a bold, fun, and highly visible move that shows how brands are getting creative with major league sports sponsorships. [S14]

🎯 THE PMM DESK

**"Storytelling Lead" is PMM, Just With a Bigger Title**
Google Ads and Anthropic are hiring for high-level "Storytelling" or "GTM Narrative" roles with massive salaries ($305k-$570k). The job descriptions? They scream product marketing: positioning, competitive claims, sales messaging, executive comms, and ensuring consistent narrative across teams.
*PMM Takeaway:* This isn't a new job; it's PMM at an executive level, validating the strategic importance of narrative and positioning. If you're a PMM, you're already building these skills, so aim high. [S7]

**"Yearly Wrapped" Builds Loyalty & Retention**
Inspired by Spotify, companies like Stakemate are building "yearly wrapped" features to show users how they engaged with the product over the past 12 months. It's a powerful way to foster loyalty and retention by tapping into nostalgia and personalized data.
*PMM Takeaway:* Consider how your product can create a personalized, shareable year-end summary. It's a product feature with huge marketing upside for stickiness and viral sharing. [S6]

🧠 PMM 101

**The concept:** Product Positioning
What it is: Product positioning is how you define your product in the minds of your target customers relative to its competition. It's about articulating the unique value you offer and why someone should choose you.
Why it matters: Strong positioning guides all your marketing, sales, and product development efforts, ensuring everyone is on the same page.
See it today: Google Ads' new "Global Narrative" role is all about defining and refreshing the product's positioning framework to ensure everyone tells the same story. [S7]
Try it: Draft a simple positioning statement for a product you know using the format: "For [target customer] who [needs/wants], [product name] is a [product category] that [key benefit/differentiator]."

🧩 PRODUCT CORNER

**Nothing's AI Earbuds Record & Transcribe Calls**
Nothing just showed off its new Ear Note AI earbuds and charging case, which come with a "Talk" button to record your own voice and a "Record" button that records and transcribes conversations. The case itself can act as a meeting recorder. It's an interesting move into AI-powered utility for personal audio, positioning these less as just headphones and more as an intelligent assistant. [S54]

🔧 TOOL DROP

**MAGI-2** — Sand AI's 480B model for generating cinematic video.
Best for: Marketers and content creators looking to quickly produce high-quality, cinematic video content using AI.
Free tier: No
Honest take: This is genuinely useful. As AI video generation gets better, tools like MAGI-2 will become essential for rapid content creation, especially for social and ad campaigns. [S9][S95]

⚡ SPEED ROUND

🚨 1Password exposed customer names and emails in a breach, though passwords are safe. [S1][S2]
💸 Tech ad spend growth is projected to slow to 8% YoY in Q4, down from 13% earlier in the year. [S3]
🤖 New York banned AI chatbot toys for kids for five years, citing safety concerns. [S44]
🗣️ Google and Anthropic are hiring "Storytelling Leads" that sound suspiciously like high-level PMM roles. [S7]
🚀 SpaceX got FCC approval to launch up to 1 million AI data center satellites for its "Starmind" initiative. [S47]
🛍️ Consumer trust in Black Friday deals is down, with many brands now starting discounts in October. [S30]
